themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what an action will do next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: All three models put a proxy or gateway in front of every agent write in the safe agent execution answers, and today they propose owning the agent entrance itself: stamping signed payment mandates at checkout, running a signed-traffic pilot, and offering agents dedicated declared endpoints.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and no one has the power to make them. The models keep saying a standard or a schema cannot fix a fight over money and self-interest.
themes.evidence: Today all three models land on incentives: agents gain by passing as human, honest disclosure needs a reward, and competing platforms must be persuaded to honor one signal; the same logic appears in the semantic layer answers, where teams defend their own numbers, and in journey orchestration, where channel owners are paid on their own conversions.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and what you are measuring often shifts while you measure it. So the first move is usually to manufacture a small truth set of your own.
themes.evidence: The models build labeled agent sessions from signed mandates and recruited pilots, a consenting panel of customers who list their devices, a fixed prompt panel for AI answers, and a count of accounts identified with certainty in B2B.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, an ad budget, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, and the parties holding the answers have little reason to open up.
themes.evidence: The consent answers say you cannot inspect an ad platform audience or prove deletion inside a trained model, the incentive answers say platforms both control and conceal the treatment, and the B2B answer says real buying talk happens in private chats no tag can reach.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: Some of the hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and implied claims, and no rule set captures that. The models keep concluding human judgment can be narrowed to a smaller, safer box, not removed.
themes.evidence: The content governance answers all say legal and brand risk turns on implied meaning that software cannot defend in an audit, so they build an approved-claims registry and constrain what the model may say; the semantic layer answers say conflicting definitions of customer are all legitimate.
